perspective: Adversarial MVP-boundary verification against all three interview transcripts and derived pipeline artifacts; separates current appointment workflow from proposed expansion.

findings.claim: Appointments are the defensible MVP center of gravity.
findings.risk: Do not expand the MVP into every HR/finance process merely because the appointment record is shared.
findings.recommendation: Keep the MVP to appointment intake/renewal confirmation, handoff, status/work queue, notes/history, change requests, and the minimum finance verification needed to process appointments.

findings.claim: A current active-appointments view is an evidenced MVP need, not optional reporting polish.
findings.risk: Active/ended semantics and source-of-truth rules remain underspecified; a dashboard without lifecycle rules could misstate payroll activity.
findings.recommendation: Include a read-oriented active-appointment summary with explicit active, stale/needs-confirmation, and ended/terminated states; preserve the upstream confirmation loop rather than inventing automatic termination.

findings.claim: Tenure/promotion tracking is a later expansion, not an MVP requirement.
findings.risk: The need for occasional provost reports is real, but the interviews do not establish a current appointment-processing dependency, owner workflow, permissions, or authoritative data source.
findings.recommendation: Exclude committee/process management and tenure/promotion workflows from MVP. At most, reserve a future extension point for read-only employment-history fields after ownership and source authority are defined.

findings.claim: Grant/chartfield work is split: appointment-linked account verification is current; full grant management is future expansion.
findings.risk: Treating active grants, startups, projections, expenses, and grant lifecycle management as MVP would turn a required appointment costing check into a separate finance product.
findings.recommendation: MVP may capture/verify chartfields, detect missing or unfunded accounts, support corrected funding, and pass costing inputs downstream. Defer grant inventory, grant budgets, reconciliation, projections, expenses, and grant creation/management.

findings.claim: Data warehouse/reporting is future architecture; targeted appointment queries and exports are the only evidenced near-term reporting need.
findings.risk: A warehouse would add integration, governance, and authority decisions not established by the interviews; current FAST/Oracle/Box sources are not reconciled into one authoritative model.
findings.recommendation: Defer a data warehouse and broad BI/reporting layer. Support only MVP list views, filters, active-appointment summaries, and CSV/Excel export over appointment data, with source limitations stated.

findings.claim: Faculty forms are not the current intake workflow; they are a future-state proposal and the mid-semester form path is not evidenced as current.
findings.risk: Building faculty self-service forms as the MVP would contradict the explicit current practice: Mayra still emails faculty and is concerned they will not complete a form.
findings.recommendation: MVP should let Mayra record and manage email-originated requests. Treat prefilled faculty forms, Qualtrics links, and enforced form-only intake as later experiments requiring adoption and ownership proof.

findings.claim: Automation is an evidenced need only where it removes repeated current steps; broad workflow automation is expansion and possible scope creep.
findings.risk: Automated emails, screening submission, offer-letter generation, Banner/FAST/Oracle integration, scheduled journeys, and automatic approvals introduce external-system, permissions, failure, and policy dependencies.
findings.recommendation: MVP automation should be bounded to templates/drafts, reminders with human confirmation, prefill/calculations, and status tracking. Defer unattended sends, auto-renewal, automatic approvals, end-to-end external submissions, and autonomous lifecycle decisions.

missing_or_ambiguous: Authoritative appointment lifecycle and active/ended definition across Oracle, worksheet, and finance summary.
Whether chartfield verification and costing are in the MVP write path or only a read/handoff surface.
Exact permissions and approval semantics for appointment changes and termination requests.
Canonical source and integration authority for Banner, Oracle, FAST, Box, Dataverse, and any warehouse.
Reminder cadence, escalation, and human approval requirements for automated email actions.
Adoption decision and owner for any future faculty self-service form.
Whether targeted exports must satisfy audit/reporting requirements beyond the appointment workflow.
